lines.text: Take a look around -- you won't find better prices anywhere.
Every item here has a story. Want to hear one?
I've traded with folk from every corner of the realm.
Supply caravans have been late. Strange things on the roads.
Stock up now. You never know what's waiting out there.
A well-equipped adventurer is a living adventurer.
I got a shipment in from the coast -- rare stuff.
Heard rumors of ancient treasures in the old ruins nearby.
Business has been good lately. Lots of travelers passing through.
I don't ask where the gold comes from. Saves everyone trouble.
Some of my finest wares came from a wandering peddler. Odd fellow.
The blacksmith and I have an arrangement -- good steel, fair price.
Word of advice: never venture out without potions.
There's a buyer for everything. Even monster parts, if you can stomach it.
Travelers bring news from far places. Not all of it good.
I've seen adventurers come and go. The smart ones stock up first.
If you find anything unusual out there, bring it to me. I pay well.
The roads used to be safer. Something has changed.
Gold spent on good gear is gold well spent.
Had a customer last week who swore he saw lights in the forest at night.
The light watches over all who walk in faith.
Your spirit carries the weight of many battles. Rest here.
The temple doors are always open to those in need.
I sense a great trial ahead of you. Stay vigilant.
Prayer alone cannot shield you -- but it helps.
The old wards around town have been weakening. I renew them each dawn.
Even the strongest warriors need healing. There is no shame in it.
Something stirs in the dark places of the world. The temple senses it.
May your path be lit and your heart be steady.
The sacred texts speak of heroes who rose in times like these.
I have tended wounds that no blade could have made. Be careful.
Faith is a shield, but wisdom is the hand that holds it.
The fallen can be restored, but the cost weighs on the soul.
There are places in this land where the light does not reach.
You carry a spark of something rare. Guard it well.
The temple has stood here for generations. It will stand for generations more.
Come to me when you are weary. Restoration is my calling.
Dreams have troubled the acolytes lately. Visions of shadow and flame.
Blessings are freely given. The light asks nothing in return.
The balance between light and dark is thinner than most realize.
I've lived here longer than most can remember.
The young ones don't listen, but the land remembers everything.
There's wisdom in the old stories, if you know how to listen.
I've seen this town through hard times before. We endure.
The forest wasn't always dangerous. Something woke up out there.
Every stranger who passes through changes this place a little.
When I was young, the roads were safe and the nights were quiet.
There are tunnels beneath the old ruins. Best not to explore them alone.
The harvest festival is coming. Good to have something to celebrate.
I've buried too many friends who thought they were invincible.
An old map in the archives shows passages that don't appear on any modern chart.
Trust the people here. We look after our own.
The river changed course twenty years ago. Nobody knows why.
Patience and preparation will take you further than any blade.
My grandmother spoke of a time when the stars shifted. Strange days followed.
Welcome, traveler. It's good to see new faces.
The town council meets at the hall. Politics, mostly. But sometimes real trouble.
There's a well at the edge of town. They say it grants visions to the worthy.
If you need direction, ask anyone here. We're a helpful lot.
History has a way of repeating itself. I hope this time we're ready.
Rest your feet. You look like you've traveled far.
A warm meal and a soft bed -- that's what we do best.
The ale's fresh and the fire's warm. What more could you want?
Had a strange group pass through last night. Wouldn't say where they were headed.
Every adventurer who's come through here has a story. Some of them even true.
You'd be surprised what people tell a barkeep after a few drinks.
The room at the end of the hall is always cold. No one books it anymore.
Business picks up when the roads get dangerous. Funny how that works.
I keep a stew going all day. Adventurers eat at odd hours.
Someone left a journal here last week. Full of sketches of creatures I've never seen.
The walls here are thick. Good for sleeping through storms -- and other things.
I hear things, running this place. Not all of it makes sense.
A traveler from the south warned me to bar the doors after sundown.
You're welcome to stay as long as you need. We've got room.
The locals come here for news as much as for drink.
I've seen all sorts walk through that door. You seem like good sorts.
Some nights, the wind carries sounds from the old ruins. Best not to think on it.
My grandfather built this inn. Said a good inn holds a town together.
Eat well and sleep deep. You'll need your strength for what's out there.
Last full moon, a wolf sat outside the door all night. Just watching.
Keep to the main roads and you'll be fine. Mostly.
We patrol the walls day and night. This town is safe.
Seen some odd tracks near the perimeter lately. Stay sharp.
Adventurers are welcome here, long as they don't cause trouble.
The captain doubled the night watch last week. Won't say why.
If you're heading out, watch for bandits on the eastern road.
We had a break-in at the storehouse. Nothing taken. Just... moved.
The townsfolk sleep easy knowing we're on watch.
I trained with the king's army before coming here. Quieter posting, usually.
Report anything unusual to the guard post. We take threats seriously.
Something set the hounds off last night. Couldn't find what it was.
Safe travels, adventurer. Come back in one piece.
The old watchtower has a clear view of the surrounding lands. Useful to know.
We don't get many visitors this time of year. Curious.
I've stood this post for years. You learn to read the wind.
There's a bounty board by the gate if you're looking for work.
The forests are crawling with creatures. Don't wander off alone.
One of our scouts went missing two nights ago. Just... gone.
Keep your weapon close and your wits closer.
I've heard tell of ancient ruins to the north. Dangerous place.
Steel and fire -- that's all I need to make something worth carrying.
Bring me materials and I'll forge something worthy of a hero.
I can tell a good blade by the ring it makes. Yours has seen some use.
The ore from the northern mines has a strange shimmer to it.
A weapon is only as good as the hand that wields it.
I've been forging since I could lift a hammer. It's in the blood.
Some metals don't behave the way they should. Old metals, from old places.
Good armor saves lives. Don't skimp on protection.
The merchant sells my work at twice what I charge. Go figure.
I found a strange symbol etched into an ingot last week. Never seen its like.
Every blade I forge, I test myself. Nothing leaves here that I wouldn't trust my life to.
Heat, hammer, patience. That's the secret to a good edge.
A traveler once brought me a shard of metal that sang when I struck it.
War is good for business, but bad for the soul. I'd rather forge plowshares.
The old forge-masters knew techniques we've lost. I'm trying to rediscover them.
Come back when your gear needs mending. I do honest work.
I temper blades under the full moon. Old habit. Might be superstition, might not.
The guard captain keeps me busy. Lots of repairs lately.
There's a vein of dark iron under the hills. Nobody dares mine it.
A strong shield has turned more battles than any magic spell.
I know every shortcut in town. Grown-ups never look in the fun places.
My friends say the old hall creaks because it remembers secrets.
If you chase butterflies long enough, you end up hearing good gossip.
I dropped my toy by the road once. It was gone before sunset.
Everybody thinks I am playing, but I notice who comes and goes.
The baker gives me warm rolls when I run errands fast enough.
There is a patch of flowers outside town that glows after dark. I am not supposed to visit it.
When the bells ring, all the little kids race to count them first.
I heard a traveler say monsters hate loud singing. Maybe we should test that.
If you ask nicely, I can point you toward the safest fence to climb.
My grandmother says brave people still need to come home for supper.
There is a window in the temple that makes rainbow light on the floor. I like standing in it.
Sometimes the guard dogs bark at nothing. I do not think it is nothing.
We pretend the empty lot is a castle until the grown-ups need it again.
I keep finding pebbles with strange marks near the gate.
A steady harvest keeps fear from taking root.
Rain came right on time this week. The fields finally look honest again.
Tracks cut across my south field at dawn, and they were not from any mule I own.
Good soil will forgive a lot, but not neglect.
We trade seed, tools, and favors out here. That is how a town lasts.
The crows keep circling the north fence. They know something is wrong before we do.
I rise before the sun and still feel behind some weeks.
Fresh milk, clean water, and a locked gate solve more problems than magic.
Last season, something trampled the corn without eating any of it.
The younger hands are strong, but they have not learned patience yet.
You can tell a storm is coming by the way the birds vanish from the hedges.
I send produce to the inn twice a week, and news always comes back with the empty cart.
There is an old well by the orchard that tastes of stone and iron now.
A sharp hoe and a sharper eye are enough to keep most trouble off the land.
I would rather mend a fence all day than let a hungry thing find a gap after dark.
The oldest answers rarely shout. You have to wait for them.
There are stories buried under this town that no archive has ever kept straight.
A calm mind notices patterns that panic walks right past.
I have seen maps that place a forgotten shrine where the road bends east.
Wisdom is not speed. It is returning with the right thing after everyone else rushed home empty-handed.
Light, shadow, iron, and memory. Those four things shape most of the trouble in this realm.
The temple bells changed tone last month. Small omens matter.
You need not be old to ask the right question.
An oath spoken in a sacred room carries further than people think.
When a town forgets its history, danger starts dressing up as novelty.
Rest when you can. Exhaustion makes fools of heroes and scholars alike.
The old carvings near the hill road are worn smooth, but their warning remains.
If a problem keeps returning, study the pattern before you study the weapon.
Most relics are only dangerous to the impatient.
A truthful answer can still arrive wrapped in poetry.
I have crossed three roads to get here, and this town still feels steadier than most.
The inn fire in this place is worth a detour all by itself.
A wagon overturned east of town. No tracks away from it, just silence.
You learn fast on the road: pack light, listen often, and never waste daylight.
I trade stories for supper when coin runs thin.
There is a mile marker north of here that faces the wrong direction now.
A clean bed after rain can make any town feel blessed.
Merchants complain in every region, but fear changes the tone of it.
I met a scout who swore the tree line moved overnight.
Your roads are kinder than the ones west of the ridge.
If you ever leave town, keep a spare pair of socks dry. That advice has saved more people than any sword.
Campfire rumors travel faster than caravans.
The moon looked wrong two nights back, like it was watching instead of shining.
Every stop teaches you who still shares bread when supplies run low.
The road ahead is passable, but I would not call it peaceful.
This town has a rhythm of its own. You hear it if you stay still long enough.
Most folks around here are willing to help if you give them reason to trust you.
Something unsettled has been moving at the edge of ordinary life lately.
Keep your eyes open and your pace steady. That advice works almost anywhere.
A kind word gets farther than people expect.
Old buildings remember more than they say.
There is always work for someone willing to see a task through.
Even a quiet street can hide an important story.
Travel safely. People here would rather greet you twice than mourn you once.
The ordinary parts of a town are what make the heroic parts worth saving.
I have learned not to dismiss strange weather or stranger timing.
A warm light in a window can do more for courage than a speech.
When trouble comes, it rarely announces itself clearly.
The people who sweep the floors usually know more than the people who own the room.
There is always another rumor, but only some of them matter.
